channel.title: DoNotKYC
channel.description: Changes to the DoNotKYC directory of no-KYC crypto platforms.

item.title: Tapbit and BloFin corrected, CoinEx sourced
item.description: Tapbit's own blog says unverified accounts can withdraw up to 2 BTC, not 10 BTC. BloFin's help center sets a Basic level limit and its terms require identity information, so it moves from None to Light. CoinEx's help center confirms the 10,000 USD daily limit without ID verification.

item.title: Advertise page: free for now, in exchange for a mention
item.description: Until we have 30 days of audience figures, a sponsored tile is free if your site mentions that DoNotKYC features you and links to donotkyc.com. We publish prices after that.

item.title: Two instant swaps added, volume and reputation lines removed
item.description: FixedFloat and ChangeNOW join the directory, each with the page of its own terms or FAQ as the source. Both ask for ID only when a swap is flagged. The "24h volume" and "Reputation" lines are gone from the listings and the API: they were not dated and partly subjective. The TikTok link is removed.

item.title: Proofreading pass and tools on the home page
item.description: Guides and API page rewritten in plainer English, the security guide loses its closing slogan in all 9 languages, and both guides now link to the matching tool pages. The home page gets a Tools section. Promotional wording and unsourced claims are removed from a few platform listings (Best Wallet, SilentSwap and some feature tags).

item.title: CoinJoin tools page
item.description: A new tools page lists Wasabi and JoinMarket with what their own sites say. It notes which services have stopped: the Wasabi coordinator in June 2024 and the archived JoinMarket repository.

item.title: Tools: operating systems, e-mail and aliases
item.description: Four more tool pages: desktop systems (Tails, Whonix, Qubes OS and more), phone systems (GrapheneOS, CalyxOS, /e/OS, LineageOS), private e-mail providers and e-mail alias services. Same entry format and same sort rule as the other tool pages.

item.title: Tools section: VPN, Tor, DNS, wallets and more
item.description: Ten new pages list the tools people use next to a no-KYC platform: VPNs, Tor and other networks, encrypted DNS, leak tests, routers, Bitcoin, hardware and Monero wallets, privacy coins and private payments. Each entry quotes the maker's own site, says what the tool asks of you and whether its code is open, and follows one sort rule. The old VPN guide now lives on the VPN page.

item.title: KYC claims corrected for 4 platforms
item.description: We compared our listings with the platforms' own policies. Changelly and StealthEX publish identity-check policies, so they no longer read "email only" or "no ID up to $700". LocalCoinSwap can ask for ID after a dispute or an alert. Bybit lets unverified accounts withdraw up to 20,000 USDT a day but asks for ID to trade. Seven listings now link the policy page they rely on.

item.title: Versioned API and security contact
item.description: The directory is now also served at /api/v1/platforms.json, one flat list with every field. A security.txt file tells researchers where to report a problem, and robots.txt names the AI crawlers that are welcome.

item.title: Cookie-free visit counter
item.description: DoNotKYC now counts visits with GoatCounter, an open-source counter with no cookies and no personal data. The privacy policy explains what it records.

item.title: Synapse back to active
item.description: synapseprotocol.com now redirects to Hypercall, the team's new product, but the Synapse bridge still works at bridge.synapseprotocol.com. The listing points there and is no longer under review.

item.title: How we make money, and a privacy policy
item.description: Two new pages explain who pays DoNotKYC (affiliate links and labelled sponsored tiles, with our advertising rules) and confirm the site collects no data about visitors.

item.title: Boltz under review: swaps suspended
item.description: Boltz suspended its swaps on 3 August 2026 and its website no longer resolves. The listing stays visible with a warning and is out of our recommendations until the service is back.

item.title: Synapse under review
item.description: synapseprotocol.com now redirects to hypercall.xyz/synapse. We are confirming the service and its address before updating the listing.

item.title: 1inch moved to 1inch.com
item.description: The listing now points to the new domain.

item.title: Weekly automatic check of every listing
item.description: Every Monday a script checks that each platform's site still answers and has not moved to another domain, and lists platforms whose last real-money test is older than 90 days.

item.title: Side-by-side comparisons
item.description: 18 comparisons of platforms that do the same job, such as MEXC vs Bybit or Bisq vs Hodl Hodl.

item.title: Site available in 9 languages
item.description: English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Turkish and Chinese.

item.title: New directory, one page per platform
item.description: Platforms are now sorted by how much identity they ask for (None, Light, Tiered), with a page each, topic pages and alternatives to exchanges that require ID. Data errors fixed for KCEX, DeGate and Boltz. Google Analytics and third-party logos removed: the site makes no request to any other service.

item.title: No-KYC crypto exchanges in 2026: limits, fees and catches
item.description: Ten exchanges that let you trade without an ID document, with limits, fees and blocked countries.

item.title: Why avoid KYC: what happens to your ID after you upload it
item.description: Exchanges keep your passport scan for years, and those files leak. Real cases and how to limit your exposure.
